senses.gloss:
Kṣviṅkā is mentioned once in the Rigveda^1 as a bird of prey.
The word also occurs in the list of victims at the Aśvamedha,
or horse sacrifice, in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā,^2 where the com-
mentary absurdly explains it as ‘a red-mouthed female ape’
(rakta-mukhī vānarī).
1) x. 87, 7.
2) v. 5, 15, 1.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 93.
